findingDetails.title: Commit-Id catalog misstates enrollment for repositories without an allocator
findingDetails.case: A repository has no allocator in its tree, but its local skilled.commitId setting is true or its recent history contains a Commit-Id. The hook policy enrolls it, while the catalog says a repository that does not ship the allocator is left alone.
findingDetails.evidence: The catalog makes the blanket no-allocator statement. cip_repo_wants_ids checks local configuration first, then toolchain markers, then Commit-Id trailers in the last 50 commits. The v4.0.0.4 changelog documents the newer enrollment rule.
findingDetails.userImpact: Readers can expect hooks to leave a repository alone when its configured policy or history actually requires Commit-Id trailers.
findingDetails.scopeProof: Compared the exact catalog sentence at line 32 with the complete enrollment function at lines 23-40 and the release-note rule at line 135.
findingDetails.recommendation: Update the catalog to describe explicit local-config and recent-history enrollment, and link the policy helper.

checklist_evidence.note: Pi source anchors and test/playbook references align for startup, persistence, and handoff. Hook test sources were inspected but not run; the all-zero case remains uncovered as recorded in R3-P1-001.

skill_agent.note: No feature-owner agent for Commit-Id hooks or Pi Fast Mode was found in the runtime agent directories; the reviewed targets are a hook set and a Pi extension.

agent_cross_runtime.note: The four runtime agent trees contain no Commit-Id or Pi Fast Mode feature agent to cross-compare; the current reviewer agent itself is loaded by the routed runtime.

feature_catalog_code.note: The Commit Identity catalog describes a repository without an allocator as left alone, but the current policy also enrolls repositories through explicit local config or Commit-Id history. Pi Fast Mode is documented in its extension README and source README, with no feature-catalog directory.

playbook_capability.note: Pi playbooks cover startup flag, persistence, and child preference. The sk-git GIT-044 playbook covers ID lookup queries, not the newer enrollment and untrusted-clone fallback behavior.

changelog_claim_audit.note: The full 475-line changelog was read and root-relative path literals were checked. Commit-Id line 135 conflicts with active R2-P0-001; Pi Fast Mode line 427 matches the source and playbooks. Other subsystem claims were enumerated, but their implementation behavior was not fully revalidated in this scoped iteration and remains deferred.
